 Daylight saving time ends Nov. 1, changing sunrise and sunset times in East Tennessee 
 Clocks fall back to standard time, shifting sunrise and sunset by about an hour. 
 By Megan Duzmal Published : Oct. 22, 2026 at 3:58 PM EDT | Updated : 6 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google What This Story Is About 
 Daylight Saving Time is ending, making Sunsets earlier. 
 What Happens Next 
 We are falling back on Nov. 1. 
 For Context 
 We are expected to stay in Standard Time through Winter unless the bill passes and permanent Daylight Time is approved. 
 KNOXVILLE, Tenn. (WVLT) - Daylight saving time ends Nov. 1, changing the timing of sunrise and sunset across East Tennessee.
 Clocks fall back from 2 a.m. to 1 a.m. on Nov. 1, marking the end of daylight saving time and the return to standard time. The change gives people an extra hour of sleep.
 Currently, sunset is just before 7 p.m. and sunrise is at almost 8 a.m.
 After the time change, sunrise will be closer to 7 a.m. and sunset will be nearing 5:30 p.m.
 Sunrise/Sunset times (WVLT) The shift means brighter mornings for the school run and morning commute, but darkness will arrive by dinner.
